newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Ruling Socialists say leading in Macedonian poll.
newsitem.headline: Ruling Socialists say leading in Macedonian poll.

text.p: The ruling Socialists said they were in the lead on Monday in a local election run-off, citing early unofficial results a day after Macedonians took part in a second round of voting.
The ruling Social Democratic Alliance said they won in 50 municipalities, while the opposition three-party coalition gained 27 districts after the second round of voting.
The remaining municipalities were shared between ethnic Albanian parties and the independent Socialist Party, they said.
In the first round in Macedonia's first local elections since independence in 1991 from former Yugoslavia on November 17, only 32 of 124 districts produced conclusive results.

The polls have been widely seen as a mid-term referendum on the government of Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski, and the opposition's campaign, which has branded the government's free-market reforms "corrupt".

But according the local electoral commission, the opposition coalition's candidate for mayor in the capital Skopje won in the second round. The success bouyed the opposition three-party coalition to say it would demand early federal elections.
The state electoral commission said polling would be repeated in 19 municipalities next Sunday, including the western Albanian-dominated town of Tetovo because of irregularities.
